title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Night Passage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Night Passage
options.lineage: Nautical charts read in night mode on a ship's bridge (ECDIS dusk/night palette)
options.thesis: The intro prints a relief layer by layer; seen from above, those layers become the depth contours of the chart the page is set on.
options.viewport: Full-bleed night chart; huge two-line name over open water bottom-left, the red dashed course runs through four real waypoints (Apopka, Orlando, Lockheed, Atlanta), email action under the name.
options.risk: A career-as-voyage reading can tip into cliché if the chart is decoration rather than the actual ground the content sits on.

raised.raise: One red thread: the plotted course is the only accent and the one path through the page.
Red marks only the waypoint in view; everything off-course stays in chart blues.
The phone repacks the chart into a vertical passage instead of shrinking the map.
Fixed stations in order: each role is a leg of one passage, read top to bottom, no carousels.

options.label: Solder Mask
options.lineage: Fabricated PCBs: matte solder mask, gold pads, white silkscreen
options.thesis: The page is a populated circuit board; each role is a component on it, traced to the next.
options.viewport: Name stacked large left; copper traces run from it into an ESP32-style component block on the right.
options.risk: Circuit-trace motifs are the most common engineering-portfolio look; familiar and easy to do badly.

options.label: Street Shout
options.thesis: His name and employers yelled at architectural scale, cropped by the frame.
options.viewport: Stacked condensed caps of the name on diagonals filling the screen, red band for the email action.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the name lands instantly) but loses audience identification: nothing in it says embedded or hardware.
options.risk: Reads as a theatre poster, not an engineer; the 3D-print intro has nothing to print into.

options.label: Jackfield Schedule
options.thesis: Roles as numbered lanes on black glass, each tied by a signal-red link line.
options.viewport: Fixed legend strip left, lanes drifting right, dominant name knocked out of a solid red plate.
options.case: Holds audience identification (hardware engineers know patch bays) but loses clarity: lane grids add reading cost for recruiters.
options.risk: Built for an Operate screen; numbered lanes fight the no-index-numbering rule and skim speed.

options.label: Safelight Bay
options.thesis: The page develops under red safelight.
options.viewport: Red-washed tray with the name emerging.
options.case: A photographic print competes with the 3D print you asked to keep; slow emergence fights skimming.
options.kept: Fixed stations in order: each role is one leg of a single passage.

options.label: Film Bloom
options.thesis: Career as a processed film strip.
options.case: No product truth to carry; recruiters do not identify with film processing.
options.kept: Accent reserved for the active frame: red marks only the waypoint in view.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull transforms a flat plane.
options.viewport: Black semicircle with one gold cord.
options.case: Fashion craft; neither axis survives fusion.
options.kept: One control carries the only accent: the course line is the single red thread.

options.label: Merz Collage
options.case: Light paper ground is ruled out; chaos fights skim speed.
options.kept: Phone layout repacks rather than scales.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer portfolio: name, one-line bio, card grid of roles, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name and bio over a row of role cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other engineering portfolio, by design.
